name: Marawah Marine Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Seagrass meadows, dugongs, turtles and wading birds in the shallow Arabian Gulf.

tip.title: Thin the seagrass
tip.text: Dugongs, green turtles and spinefoot all graze seagrass. Set Narrowleaf seagrass to -100% and watch them, then the tiger shark above them.

sources.title: Gulf News: Marawah is UAE's first biosphere reserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Shallow, clear water lets light reach seagrass beds; Halophila ovalis can die within about 30 days if light is cut off.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead seagrass, mangrove leaves and animal remains, returning nutrients to the sediment.

nodes.name: Narrowleaf seagrass
nodes.desc: A seagrass resident in the Persian Gulf that forms dense meadows and tolerates a wide salinity range. Dugongs favour Halodule.
A low-fibre, nitrogen-rich seagrass that dugongs prefer. It declines fast when light is lost.
One of the few mangroves of the arid Arabian coast, growing in salt flats with aerial roots that work in flooded mud.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton and microalgae
nodes.desc: Drifting and mud-surface algae such as diatoms that feed sponges and filter-feeding flamingos.
Grazes seagrass, favouring Halophila and Halodule. The Gulf holds the second-largest dugong population and the UAE bans hunting.
Adults are mostly herbivores that graze seagrasses and some algae in shallow coastal water.
Sponges make up most of its diet, along with algae, seagrass and mangrove fruits and seeds.
Filters small prey, algae and diatoms from shallow salty mud and lagoons by stirring the mud with its feet.

nodes.name: Sponges
nodes.desc: Filter feeders of reefs and hard bottoms that strain tiny particles from the water; the main food of hawksbills.
Stalks shallows for fish, crustaceans and molluscs, and regularly takes mudskippers on the coast.
A wader with a heavy bill built for crabs; it breeds in burrows in sandy banks around the Gulf.
Fish-eating raptor that dives feet first onto live fish; about 99% of its diet is fish.
Wide-ranging coastal predator that eats fish, sea turtles and dugongs; dugongs often carry scars from shark attacks.
